correctness.rationale: The graph-flow quotient identification is proved via dual equality of Lipschitz and weighted-edge constraints. In a finite cactus edge-disjoint cycle indicators form a full basis for the incidence kernel, so quotient blocks split. For any quotient operator the norm is max of the images of weighted ℓ1 edge generators, by quotient metricity. Retained generators have ratio at most 1; omitted cycle generators have norm exactly the two-level weighted median min(W_C,L_C-W_C). A nonzero projection has norm at least 1, giving equality. For unit weights, prefix cycle-edge counts sweep each integer 0 through m-1, proving ordering independence. An independently coded exact transportation-minimization test passed 8 graphs and 128 subsets; its finiteness is not construed as proof.

Direct source comparisons include arXiv:1207.1583, Hájek–Pernecká Theorem 3.1, arXiv:1910.03625 Theorem 3.1, arXiv:1905.13188 Theorem 5, arXiv:2305.12582, and arXiv:2601.16859 Corollary 4.2; these give nearby existence, quotient structure or transportation-demand norm facts, but not this all-subset operator calculation. residual_risks: The complete original Cabrelli–Molter 1995 journal article was not examined; only its abstract and an explicit citation to its weighted-cycle result were available. Its subject is the transportation metric, but uninspected additional claims leave bibliographic risk.

value.rationale: Exact norm profile for every coordinate suppression in natural explicit spanning-tree bases over the entire finite weighted cactus class, extending arbitrary numbers of cycles and nongeodesic edges. The unit-weight specialization determines maximal partial-sum and suppression constants for every order/tree and a sharp monotonicity structural criterion: absence of cycles with at least 4 edges. This addresses basis stability and cycle-induced loss of unconditional control, a motivated finite-dimensional Banach-space invariant rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
